The structure is described in the body-centered tetragonal space group I-4m2, number 119, with Hall symbol I -4 -2. The supplied input cell is not the conventional tetragonal cell: it is a smaller primitive-like cell with all three edge lengths equal to 6.19776332 Å and interaxial angles of 139.7884713°, 139.7884713°, and 58.17461593°. This input cell contains five atoms with the declared composition Pr1Ga3Pd1. Fractional coordinates in this input frame are related to the standard I-4m2 frame by q_standard = P q_input + s, where the origin shift s is (0, 0, 0) and the matrix P has rows (0.5, -0.5, 0.5), (-0.5, 0.5, 0.5), and (-0.5, -0.5, 0.5). Thus the input cell can be recovered exactly by applying the inverse of that transformation to the standard description.

In the standard frame, the praseodymium atoms occupy Wyckoff orbit 2a at the fixed position (0, 0, 0), giving two symmetry-equivalent Pr sites per conventional cell. Gallium is distributed over two crystallographically distinct sublattices. The first is Wyckoff orbit 4e, with representative position (0, 0, z) and z = 0.384387; this orbit has multiplicity four and therefore contributes four Ga atoms related by the body-centered tetragonal symmetry operations. The second gallium sublattice is Wyckoff orbit 2c at the fixed position (0, 1/2, 1/4), with multiplicity two. Palladium occupies Wyckoff orbit 2d at the fixed position (0, 1/2, 3/4), also with multiplicity two.

Taken together, the conventional standard cell contains 2 Pr, 6 Ga, and 2 Pd atoms, while the supplied input cell contains the reduced five-atom content Pr1Ga3Pd1 because of the nonstandard cell choice. All positional values are reported to six decimal places where applicable, and no precision corrections are required: the listed coordinates already represent the input geometry without any displacement from rounded or idealized positions.
